name: Call Partner Rook
description: Four-player Rook variant using all 57 cards. Deal 13 each and 5 to the nest; players bid in multiples of 5 (dealer first). High bidder takes the nest, discards five, names trump, and calls a partner by naming a card not in hand; that card's holder is the secret partner (or bidder plays alone if holding it). Twelve tricks; follow color; Rook ranks between 11 and 10 in trump. First to 500 wins.

history.origins: Call Partner Rook is a four-player Rook variant from the United States. Partner is determined each hand by the bidder naming a card; whoever holds it plays with the bidder for that hand.
timeline: 1906: Rook deck introduced by Parker Brothers; games such as Call Partner developed as local variants using the full 57-card deck and partner-calling.
history.cultural: Played in North American communities where Rook is popular, including Eastern Kentucky and Mennonite communities in Southern Ontario, Manitoba, Pennsylvania, and Ohio. The Rook deck was originally marketed to groups that avoided standard playing cards.
history.evolution: Rook was introduced by Parker Brothers in 1906. Call Partner evolved as one of many local Rook variants, using the full 57-card deck and the call-partner mechanism; it is distinct from Kentucky Rook and from the booklet games supplied with the deck.

setup.players: Four players; two teams per hand (bidder and called partner vs others).
setup.dealing: One card at a time to each player until each has 13; first card goes to the player to dealer's left. After each of the first five rounds of the deal, one card is placed face down in the center to form the five-card nest.

rules.objective: As the bidding team, take at least the number of card points you bid; as the opposing team, score the points you take. First player to reach 500 or more points wins.
rules.gameplay: Dealer deals 13 cards to each player and 5 to the nest (first card to dealer's left; after each of the first five rounds one card to the nest). Players bid in multiples of 5, dealer first, clockwise; each bid must be higher than the last, and a player who passes cannot bid again. When three have passed, the fourth is the high bidder. The bidder picks up the nest without showing it (18 cards), discards any five face-down to form a new nest, names trump (a color), and calls for a partner by naming a card not in hand; whoever holds that card is the bidder's partner for the hand (secret until the card is played), and the other two form the opposing team (if the bidder holds the called card, the bidder plays alone). Player to the left of the bidder leads to the first trick; players must follow the led color if able; the Rook counts as trump. Highest trump wins the trick, or if no trump was played, highest card of the led color. Winner of each trick leads next; winner of the last trick takes the five discarded nest cards. Each team totals card points from its tricks; if the bidder's team made at least the bid, each member scores the team's points; otherwise the bidder's team subtracts the bid from their score. The opposing team always scores the points they took. Game ends when a player reaches 500 or more; highest score wins.
keyRules: Bid in multiples of 5; dealer bids first; three passes end the auction. Bidder takes nest, discards five, names trump, calls partner by naming a card. Follow color; Rook ranks between 11 and 10 in trump. Last trick winner takes nest cards. Card points: 1=15, 14=10, 10=10, 5=5, Rook=20, last trick=20. First to 500 wins.

strategy.basic: Bid when you have good trump and point cards; avoid overbidding. Call a card you do not hold to find a partner.
strategy.intermediate: Track which point cards have been played; infer partner when the called card appears. Lead trump to pull opponents' trumps when your side has length.
strategy.advanced: Optimize the call to maximize chance your partner has the card; coordinate with partner through carding when identity is revealed.
tips: If you hold the called card, do not reveal it until it helps your side.
Winning the last trick gives your team the nest points (20).

scoring.description: Card points: 1=15, 14=10, 10=10, 5=5, Rook=20; last trick=20 (200 per hand). Bidder's team scores its points if they make the bid, else subtract the bid; opposing team always scores its points. Individual scores; first to 500 wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Rook for four: bidder calls partner by naming a card; first to 500 wins.
